title: Picking a cut or a first clip on the timeline answers inside 50 ms
goal: A click on a cut between two pieces, or the first click on a clip when nothing was picked, still keeps the app busy for about 75 ms while the right hand panel swaps one set of sections for another. Bring both under the video success line of 50 ms without changing what the panel shows.
notes:
Carried from clicking-a-clip-on-the-timeline-answers-at-once (2026-10-06), which brought a cut click from 95-131 ms to 70-85 and a piece after a cut from ~121 (once the panel followed the pick) to 34-73, and left these. Measured by ablation on the five minute Retina talk with captions (Scripts/playtest/perf/clip-click-cost-walk.json, front): a cut click is one pass of ~70 ms: removing the clip's 9 sections (~40 ms of section contents, spread with no single culprit: each group of sections ~5 ms, Captions ~12-15; ~20 ms the section shells: CollapsibleSection chrome, headers, geometry readers) plus ~12-25 ms of pick, timeline and menu bar (EditorCommands body). A first pick from nothing (canvas sections Canvas/Time/Captions to the clip's) is ~75-85 ms in the click's pass: nopanel 35, blank section bodies 58-61. Tried and rejected: keeping departed sections built but hidden (worse: 120-145 ms, the layout and accessibility cost follows the controls); dock height budget by reference (no change). The trailing accessibility pass (AccessibilityNode.updateFocus walking every AppKit-backed control) scales with controls added or removed in a pass; PanelRowsArrival is the tool that split it for Captions. Probe/dev walk markers (one NSView per playtestField/Control) add ~15-30 ms to those passes. Profile with xcrun xctrace record --template "Time Profiler" --attach <probe pid>.

Rescoped 2026-10-07 by the runner. Original acceptance: A click on a cut and a first pick of a clip each hold the main thread under 50 ms in nine of ten clicks of clip-click-cost-walk over three runs, none over 100 ms | The panel still shows the cut (Edit point, Transition) after a cut click and the clip after a piece click, in the click's own frame | an-editing-session-walk and clip-click-cost-walk stay green. Not met on the probe: it hangs the markers by design, so its numbers did not move (first 78-86, cut 73-81), and with the markers off a first pick is ~56 and a cut ~53, still over 50. The 50 ms line, the probe's own-marker overstatement, and the measured levers are carried by a-first-clip-pick-and-a-cut-click-answer-inside.
acceptance: The dev app no longer hangs the walk markers: only a probe launched with a walk does, proven by a unit test of the rule and by every walk that reads markers staying green
With the markers off, as the dev app now runs, a first clip pick and a cut click each hold the main thread clearly less than before on clip-click-cost-walk (measured on a stand-in build)

log.note: Baseline on the probe (clip-click-cost-walk, HEAD a1ffc73f): first pick 78-86 ms, cut 73-81, piece after a cut 28-59, piece to piece 17-18. Reproduced the 75 ms both ways.

Cause, measured: (1) the walk's own markers. A view census 0.35s after a pick: 1589 views in the window, ~790 of them markers (PanelTargetView 159, HelpAnchorView 84, HoverTargetView 80, ReadoutAnchorView 43, each with its own SwiftUI AppKitPlatformViewHost). Removing every marker but the walk's timeline ones: first pick 53-58, cut 51-56 (-20..25 ms). Dock markers only: first 71-78, cut 56-67, so the rest of the window's markers count too. (2) SwiftUI's accessibility focus walk: AccessibilityNode.updateFocusResponder runs once per accessibility node whose focus attachment changes (~50 per first pick, counted with an lldb breakpoint), and each run visits every responder in the window (ViewRendererHost.focusResponder, mostly swift_conformsToProtocol). ~30 ms of an 80 ms first pick with markers, ~20 of ~55 without. It is live for real users: an out-of-process accessibility client queried the probe over MIG 1.8 s after launch (no harness call involved). (3) On a first pick, Canvas is the only section that leaves (with the playhead on a cut the nothing-picked dock already shows Edit point, Transition, Time, Captions, Transitions); every CollapsibleSection body re-runs on every arrival pass (68 bodies over one pick) because its closures defeat diffing.

Tried: markers sizing themselves without Auto Layout (sizeThatFits) - no change; markers .accessibilityHidden - no change; keeping removed marker views (and their hosts) alive 0.3 s so they dealloc out of the click's pass - cut 75 -> 67, first pick unchanged (not shipped: it retains SwiftUI's own host view past dismantle); section headers skipping their body when title/chip are unchanged (EquatableView) - about -2..3 ms (not shipped: stale closures over the section list and stale header notes need care); headers not focusable - focus updates 54 -> ~50, no real change (reverted, keyboard access needs them).

Adversarial review: nothing a person sees changes; the dev app is the same app with ~800 invisible views gone, so every panel swap there is 20-25 ms lighter (piece to piece 18 -> ~11, piece after a cut ~40 -> ~25). Risk was walks losing their markers: the switch is a static read of the launch arguments, true for every walk run, unit tested (AppFlavor.hangsWalkMarkers), and the walks that read every marker kind stayed green: clip-click-cost, an-editing-session, segment-tooltips, readout-fields, text-height-readout, one-unit-word, panel-edge-column, history-tooltips, panel-start-margin. Scripts/test.sh 11666 passed. No audit: no visible surface changed. Commit 8388ac09.

The dev app no longer hangs the walk's ~800 invisible marker views (only a probe launched with a walk does): AppFlavor.hangsWalkMarkers + PlaytestMarkers.areHung, also gating the panel start/edge geometry probes. Markerless stand-in on clip-click-cost-walk: first pick ~80 -> ~56 ms, cut ~78 -> ~53, piece after a cut ~40 -> ~25, piece to piece 18 -> ~11. Probe numbers unchanged by design. Original 50 ms line not met; rescoped, causes measured and logged, carried by a-first-clip-pick-and-a-cut-click-answer-inside. Tests 11666 passed; 9 marker-reading walks green. Commits 8388ac09, b09c1d56.
